title: Prediction of Patient Satisfaction after Treatment of Chronic Neck Pain with Mulligan's Mobilization
summary: A prospective cohort of 80 patients treated for chronic neck pain was used to evaluate several prediction algorithms, ending in a logistic/machine-learning model. STAI and lateral-flexion range of motion were the selected predictors of patient satisfaction, and the corrected AUC was 0.676. This is a modest exploratory prediction of a patient-reported outcome, not evidence of treatment efficacy or a validated decision tool, and it does not establish independent replication or real-world benefit.
ai_technology: Logistic regression, GBM and random forest
organization: Universidad Rey Juan Carlos; Universidad Europea de Madrid; Universidad Europea de Canarias; Universidad Autónoma de Madrid

evidence.tested: The publisher full text (Methods and Results, reviewed in Chrome) describes a prospective cohort of 80 patients treated for chronic neck pain and evaluates multiple prediction algorithms, with a final logistic/ML model. It identifies STAI and lateral-flexion range of motion as selected predictors of patient satisfaction; corrected AUC was 0.676. Approve narrowly as a modest exploratory patient-reported outcome prediction, not evidence of treatment efficacy or a validated decision tool.
evidence.unknown: The source-checked evidence does not establish broader external validity or prospective benefit. Affiliation was not available in the retrieved trusted primary metadata.
evidence.ai_role: a prespecified algorithm suite was trained/evaluated on the prospective 80-patient clinical cohort, with a final logistic/ML prediction model. The learned model operation links baseline clinical/psychological measures to post-treatment satisfaction.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
